items.title: Meta ads is now available in AWS Quick
items.excerpt: AWS Quick now has a Meta ads AI connector. Meta advertisers can use natural language in Quick to create, manage, and analyze campaigns while staying connected to the Meta ad management network, and combine Meta ad data with first- and third-party sources to build dashboards, documents, slide decks, and automated workflows.

items.title: Robin Desktop v0.3.20
items.excerpt: **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/langchain-ai/open-swe/compare/desktop-ui-3c41ba856817eac5530cf2b2486a5e3c33c0a610...desktop-v0.3.20

items.title: New in AWS Quick: More capable flows, an updated web experience, and agents that work together
items.excerpt: AWS Quick is the AI workspace built only for work. Today we're releasing updates that help your team get more done: build and run business-process flows in chat, triage your day in the updated web app, get more complete answers from multiple agents at once, and connect new data sources like Meta ads and Amplitude.

items.title: Cut self-hosted LLM cost and latency with the distributed KV caching agent skill
items.excerpt: Self-hosting LLMs on GPUs means paying to recompute the same context on every turn. Distributed KV caching with Amazon ElastiCache can cut inference cost by up to 40% and time to first token by up to 80%. This post walks through the distributed KV caching skill in the Agent Toolkit for AWS, which evaluates and sets up the cache from your coding agent.

items.title: Introducing managed cluster extensions for observability and user management in Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Slurm
items.excerpt: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod now offers managed cluster extensions for observability and user management, bringing declarative, API- and console-driven configuration to the software running on Slurm cluster nodes. This post explains how the extensions work and follows a platform team through a quarter of running a shared Slurm cluster with them.

items.title: Introducing Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Global Inference Gateway: One endpoint across Regions and clusters
items.excerpt: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod introduces the Global Inference Gateway, one managed endpoint that routes inference requests across your HyperPod clusters in one Region or across Regions. It picks the best cluster, fails over automatically, and authenticates every request with SigV4 and IAM over AWS PrivateLink.

items.title: How Standard Bank Group automates AI risk assessment for generative AI
items.excerpt: Standard Bank Group automated the evidence behind its generative AI approval gates. Working with AWS Professional Services, the bank built an assessment in its own AWS account that scores each use case against international AI standards and its own policies using LLM-as-a-judge on Amazon Bedrock, giving risk committees consistent, traceable evidence.

items.title: Announcing Amazon Textract Insights: Verifiable generative AI for documents
items.excerpt: Announcing the general availability of Amazon Textract Insights, a new generative AI feature of Amazon Textract. Describe the fields you need in natural language, submit a document or a mixed packet, and receive structured results with a confidence score and page-level grounding for each value, with no model training required.

items.title: Introducing enhanced infrastructure observability in Amazon SageMaker HyperPod
items.excerpt: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod now offers enhanced observability to help you diagnose GPU training issues faster. It brings together diagnostic and profiling capabilities for training workloads on both Amazon EKS and Slurm orchestrators, pinpointing issues across GPU, network, and host layers.

items.title: Combatting adversarial distillation
items.excerpt: OpenAI’s layered approach to adversarial distillation combines model training, safeguards, detection, and enforcement to protect against capability extraction.

items.title: Amazon SageMaker Inference: 2026 launches in review, part 2
items.excerpt: This second installment reviews 13 more Amazon SageMaker AI inference launches from 2026, spanning configuration recommendations, fitting more models onto each GPU, serving models too large for one instance, cross-Region routing, and post-launch tuning, bringing the year's total to 26.

items.title: Use Kimi Code CLI with models on Amazon Bedrock
items.excerpt: Kimi Code CLI v2.7.0 adds a native Amazon Bedrock provider, so you can connect the open source coding agent to models like Kimi K3.1 Pro using your standard AWS credential chain (named profiles or SSO) instead of a separate API key. This post shows how to configure the provider and send your first request.

items.title: Enable AI agents to pay for AWS Marketplace x402 products with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments
items.excerpt: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments now supports AWS Marketplace, so agents can discover and buy x402-enabled products, APIs, data, and content and pay in USD on the developer's AWS bill, with no stablecoin wallets or API keys. This post walks through a research agent that finds a tool, pays per request through AWS Billing, and answers with sources.

items.title: How the BMW Group governs hundreds of agents across thousands of developers
items.excerpt: When hundreds of agents serve thousands of developers, governance cannot be an afterthought. The BMW Group shares the practices and patterns its R&D teams use to build, govern, and operate AI agents at enterprise scale without sacrificing speed, quality, or compliance.

items.title: Run your whole selling business in AWS Quick
items.excerpt: Most sellers do not need another AI product to learn. They need the tools and information they already use brought together, so they can see what is happening in their business and act on it.

items.title: Amazon SageMaker AI now detects latency drift, idle GPUs, and missed optimizations on your inference endpoints
items.excerpt: Amazon SageMaker AI now monitors your generative AI inference endpoints by default and tells you when a change could improve performance or lower cost. It tracks latency, GPU utilization, and serving configuration, then sends a finding through AWS Health with a one-click path to benchmark alternatives in SageMaker Studio before you apply any change.

items.title: Inside Amazon Connect Talent: The science of structured AI interviews
items.excerpt: For organizations hiring hundreds or thousands of people, every interview presents the same challenge: How do you give candidates a consistent opportunity to demonstrate their skills while gathering the evidence needed to make informed hiring decisions? Structured behavioral interviews offer a research-backed approach to this challenge. They use consistent, job-related questions and clear scoring criteria […]

items.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness adds Strands harness defaults, built-in tools, and lifecycle hooks
items.excerpt: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness now runs on the open-source Strands harness, bringing a recommended model, task-oriented defaults, automatic prompt caching, proactive context management, and new built-in tools. It also adds lifecycle hooks so you can run deterministic allow or deny checks at defined points in the agent loop.

items.title: Amazon Polly launches voice cloning: A unique voice for your brand
items.excerpt: Voice cloning in Amazon Polly is now generally available. Give Amazon Polly a few minutes of recordings from a consenting speaker, and it builds a custom voice that reads new text in that speaker's voice. Cloned voices run on the Amazon Polly generative engine and support seven languages.

items.title: Optimize AI economics on Amazon Bedrock with Accenture’s sequenced approach
items.excerpt: As enterprises scale AI on Amazon Bedrock, token spend can grow even as per-token prices fall. This post walks through six composable optimization levers, shows how Accenture applied them across four client engagements, and recommends a sequence for cutting AI token spend on your own workloads.

items.title: From learning to leaderboard: How Cisco upskilled 1,200 engineers in agentic AI with AWS AI League
items.excerpt: Cisco and AWS used Cisco Transformation Fest and AWS AI League to turn hands-on AI learning into a culture of building. A Cisco engineer won the 2025 AWS AI League global title and 1,200 engineers competed in 2026. This post shares Cisco's journey, lessons from the 2026 winning agent built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and how to host your own league.

items.title: Keep inference running through regional capacity shortfalls with cross-Region inference routing in Amazon SageMaker AI
items.excerpt: Cross-Region inference routing in Amazon SageMaker AI gives your application one invocation path across the endpoints and inference components you already run, in one or more AWS Regions and AWS accounts. The router prefers its own Region and shifts new requests to another destination only when the local one can't serve reliably.

items.title: Introducing Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API
items.excerpt: Give your agents access to hundreds of tools while using fewer tokens with Tool Retrieval, now in preview in the Gemini API.

items.excerpt: Walter Isaacson joins Google to discuss how history’s greatest innovators inspire creativity and human judgment in the AI age. Watch the episode.

items.excerpt: Learn how OpenAI built the Performance Factory, a system of Codex-powered workflows that finds and fixes performance issues to help keep ChatGPT fast.
